evidence: frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/core.tsx:257 — the `/settings/privacy` route renders `<PrivacySettingsPage />` directly with NO `<ProtectedRoute>` wrapper, inconsistent with every sibling `/settings/*` route in the same settingsRoutes() aggregator (oauth-grants:259-266, sessions:268-275, members:277-284, integrations:286-293, portal-webhooks:298-305, notifications:307-314, notifications/advanced:316-323 are all wrapped in `<ProtectedRoute>`). `/settings/accessibility` (core.tsx:255) is likewise unwrapped.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/privacy/pages/PrivacySettingsPage.tsx:24-62 — the page is GDPR consent/data-export management. On mount its useEffect(loadSettings) unconditionally fires two user-scoped requests (`gdprFetch('/api/v1/gdpr/privacy')` and `gdprFetch('/api/v1/gdpr/export/history')`). It reads `user` via useAuth (L26) but never guards/redirects on an unauthenticated session.

Impact: an anonymous visitor hitting /settings/privacy triggers unauthenticated GDPR fetches that 401, landing them on an inline error surface instead of the login redirect every other protected settings screen gives. Not a data leak (backend enforces auth), but a broken auth-gating path and a UX regression; the privacy screen in particular should match the ProtectedRoute convention. Landable frontend-only fix: wrap the `/settings/privacy` (and `/settings/accessibility` if it needs auth) Route element in `<ProtectedRoute>` like its siblings.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:244-258 — parseValidationDetails() stores the backend's raw `detail.message` (untranslated English) into the per-field validationErrors Map, which is surfaced to users via getFieldError() (L466-471) and formatValidationErrors() (L432-438). The module docstring (L7-10) states user-facing copy is resolved through react-i18next; validation field messages bypass that contract and leak server English into sk/cs/de/hu/pl locales.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/errorHandler.ts:447-457 — formatFieldName() builds user-facing field labels by splitting snake_case and Title-Casing in English (e.g. 'street_name' -> 'Street Name'), so the label prefix in formatValidationErrors() is also hardcoded English rather than i18n-resolved.

Impact: i18n gap on form validation feedback — a known-English-leak class the repo has otherwise fixed in the sibling describeError.ts (which deliberately keeps raw server text only as secondary `detail`). Low severity (+1); fix by keying validation messages/field labels through the i18n catalogue (or at minimum documenting that detail.message is intentionally raw).
